about: Compiler bugs that the human has ruled on, each with a reproducer that was run on the
pinned compiler when it was added. The decision log (decision-log.md) holds the reasoning.
A ruling is confirmed when the human has discussed the intended semantics with Modular's
developers; the outcome goes in `confirmation`. If a ruling turns out wrong, the human
`upstream.status`: unfiled, filed, fixed-upstream. Only the human files upstream reports.
`nightly` records the last check of the reproducer on a Mojo nightly, before the human meets Modular.

bugs.title: xs[i] = f(xs) stores into a stale element when f grows or shrinks xs
bugs.reproducer:
def bump(mut xs: List[Int]) -> Int:
    xs.append(7)
    return 5


def main():
    var xs: List[Int] = [1, 2]
    xs[0] = bump(xs)
    print(xs[0], len(xs))
bugs.compiler: accepts and prints `1 3`: it locates xs[0] before the call, the append reallocates, and the store of 5 is lost

nightly.result: accepts and prints `1 3`; AddressSanitizer reports heap-use-after-free, as on 1.2.0

bugs.title: a struct initialized field by field destroys a field that was never set
bugs.reproducer:
struct Res(Movable):
    var id: Int

    def __init__(out self, id: Int):
        self.id = id

    def __del__(deinit self):
        print("drop", self.id)


struct Two(Movable):
    var a: Res
    var b: Res

    def __init__(out self):
        self.a = Res(1)
        self.b = Res(2)


def main():
    var t: Two
    t.a = Res(1)
    print(t.a.id)
bugs.compiler: prints `1`, `drop 1`, `drop 0`: it runs the destructor of t.b, which was never initialized
bugs.model: destroys only the fields that were initialized: prints `1`, `drop 1`

bugs.title: @fieldwise_init fails inside a struct cycle through a List when the decorated struct is declared first, where the hand-written initializer compiles
bugs.compiler: rejects: "field 'bs' has non-'Deinitable' type 'List[B]'". With B's initializer written by hand as `def __init__(out self, var a: A): self.a = a^`, it compiles and prints `1`. With A declared first, 1.2.0 rejects the decorated form with "invalid implicit move: unexpected keyword argument 'move'"
bugs.model: accepts it, as it accepts the hand-written form, and prints `1`

nightly.result: partly fixed. The A-first form now compiles and prints `1`, and so does the form where both structs are @fieldwise_init with A first. The reproducer above, with B declared first, is still rejected with the same non-'Deinitable' error; its hand-written form compiles
